body:
A session can now read any project from a map built from its code instead of hand-written docs: one screen that lists the areas and what each is for, a card per area, and a table of the joins between screens, routes, schemas and tables. On your French repo it flags all three bugs from the 11-25 audit on its own, and it refuses to say it is current once the code has changed.

### What it writes
- **overview.md**: one screen. Areas sorted by size, each with what it is for (the first sentence of its entry file's leading comment or docstring), files, lines and entry points (Next pages and routes, `__main__` scripts). Then the features that cross areas (`jeu` spans app/api, app/enseignant, app/jeu, components, lib, scripts, tests), the project's own generators, and the flags.
- **areas/<area>.md** and **areas/feature-<word>.md**: a "Start here" line (screens, write routes, what it leans on most), then the files with line counts, exports and what each is, what it imports and what imports it (through `export *` barrels, so `@/lib/moteur` resolves to `lib/moteur/faussaire.ts`), its tests, the routes it serves or calls, its generators and its flags.
- **joins.md**: one row per route: who calls it (file:line), the fields sent, the fields the Zod schema accepts (including discriminated-union members), the handler, the Drizzle tables it touches (directly, or one step away through what it imports), its tests, and its CSRF/auth guards.
- **map.json**: `things` (files, areas, features, routes, schemas, tables, generators), `links` (imports, calls, handled-by, validates, touches, tests, generates), each with a check that reruns, `flags`, plus the commit, a per-file fingerprint and the same rows as the pages.

### The flags
- **dropped-field**: a field the UI sends, either at the top level or inside a union member found by its discriminant (`type: "corrompre"`), that the schema does not declare. Zod's default mode silently strips it. When a handler tries several schemas in turn (creation, then vote), it counts the union of their fields.
- **no-csrf / no-auth**: a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE whose handler body calls nothing that looks like an origin or CSRF check, or nothing that looks like an auth check. The patterns can be overridden per project. Login, signup, cron and webhook routes are treated as public. A middleware that checks the origin covers every route.
- **never-read**: a field of a type declared in a screen that calls a GET route, which no screen reads anywhere.
- **uncalled**: a route nothing calls (vercel.json crons count as callers).
- **big-file**: a file over 1,500 lines.
- **generator-failed**: a project generator that exits non-zero.

### The real case: ~/french, read-only
Run as `kit.py map --root ~/french --out <scratch> --config <scratch>/french-map.json`, where the scratch config holds `{"map":{"generators":[{"name":"carte","run":"pnpm -s carte","area":"lib/moteur"}]}}`. You approved running `pnpm carte` in check mode. It printed `CARTE: à jour` (exit 0) and its output is linked from the game's card.

```
## Flags at the joins: 1 dropped-field, 2 no-csrf, 4 never-read, 8 uncalled, 6 big-file
- dropped-field POST /api/jeu/action: `action.feuilles` is sent (app/jeu/ronde.tsx:2209, type "corrompre") but the schema Corps silently drops it
- no-csrf POST /api/enseignant/jeu/equipes writes with no CSRF check
- no-csrf POST /api/enseignant/tableau writes with no CSRF check
- never-read `activiteParFenetre` (type Vue, app/jeu/ronde.tsx:61) comes from GET /api/jeu/[id]/etat but no screen reads it
- never-read `activiteParDomaine` (same)
```
Game card, first lines: `Start here: screens app/jeu/ronde.tsx, app/enseignant/jeu/faussaire.tsx; writes POST /api/jeu/action, ...; leans on lib/moteur/faussaire.ts, db/schema.ts.`

Beyond the audit, it also found a second write route with no CSRF check (`/api/enseignant/tableau`) and three routes that nothing calls (`/api/eleves/[id]/*`).

### What it cannot read comes first
The Harmonize run (the orchestrator's `real_project`) showed the map staying silent on 568 Kotlin files it has no reader for, and its overview said "flags: none", which reads as "nothing wrong". Now any source file in a language without a reader (Kotlin, Java, Swift, Go, Rust, SQL, shell, Power BI and about 30 more) is counted. The overview's third line says how many there are and in which languages, and how many source files the map actually covers, for example `NOT READ: 33 source file(s), no reader yet: 28 SQL, 5 shell. This map covers 817 of 850 source files; its flags say nothing about the rest.` Each language is also an `unread` flag naming its folders, and map.json lists the files under `unread`. A Kotlin reader is a natural next reader for M4.

### Fresh or refused
`kit.py map --check` hashes every code file (a file whose size and modification time have not changed is not reread) and reruns every link's check, for example "ronde.tsx still contains `/api/jeu/action`", plus each generator. Editing a file gives `STALE: 1 code file(s) changed since the map was built from <commit>: <file>` and exit 1.

### Where this sits in your design (comment m1-owner-map-design)
map.json is already shaped as things, links and flags, and every link has a check that `kit.py map --check` reruns. On ~/french that is 2,565 checks, all passing. Code is the first reader. M4 can add Power BI, documents or any folder as another entry in `READERS` that returns the same things and links. M2 (install draws the first map) and M3 (each part's done checks its stretch and adds its new parts) can both call `kit.py map` and `--check` as they are. A thing only a browser sees would need a new check kind (a probe with its last confirmed date); that is not built here.

handoff: `kit.py map` (scripts/kit_map.py, copied to .kit/kit_map.py by install) writes .board/map/{overview.md, areas/*.md, joins.md, map.json}. map.json is things, links and flags, and each link carries a check (`contains`, `imports`, `exists`, or `run` for a generator) that `map --check` reruns along with the per-file fingerprint. A new reader is one more entry in `kit_map.READERS` returning the same per-file facts. Project settings live under `map` in .kit/config.json (or `--config`): `generators` (commands, each with an optional `area`), `csrf` / `auth` / `public` regexes, and `areas` globs. Running it for real on harmonize: `python3 -I .kit/kit.py map --root <clone> --out <scratch>`.
not_checked: The audit's other half of bug 3 (the teams route does not check that its members belong to the group, and has no transaction) is not something the map detects: it flags the missing CSRF check only.
The "never read" check also flags `reDemande` and `etatRegle` in app/entrainer/seance.tsx; I did not confirm whether those are real leaks or harmless leftovers.
The real-project dry run on anlonlt/harmonize is the orchestrator's to do (lesson K2).
Readers cover Python (ast) and TS/JS (Next routes, Zod, Drizzle, fetch). Express, Pydantic and GraphQL are not read yet.

task:
Build `kit.py map`: a map of any project, generated from its code, never written by hand, that a session reads in one screen and zooms into.

Why: in the owner's French repo the game ("jeu") never fit in a session's context. It had about 7,100 lines of hand-written docs about it, ordered by date, partly stale (its main doc predates 149 of the 168 commits touching the game), with two docs each claiming to be the authority. The one part that stayed true was generated from code and checked by a test (`pnpm carte`, the engine's actions). The 11-25 audit found three serious bugs, all at the joins between layers, which no doc showed: the UI sends a `feuilles` field that the API's Zod schema silently drops; the projection still sends students data the screen no longer shows; a teams route has no CSRF check and no membership check.

1. `kit.py map [--root DIR] [--out DIR]` writes the map, in scripts/kit.py and scripts/kit_map.py: `overview.md` (one screen, at most 60 lines: the areas of the project, what each is for in one line taken from code, its size, its entry points), one card per area (files with line counts, exports, what it imports and what imports it, its tests), and `map.json` with the same facts. Default out: `.board/map/`.
2. Readers for Python (ast: functions, classes, imports) and TypeScript/JavaScript (exports, imports, Next routes under the app folder with their methods, Zod objects, Drizzle tables), without installing anything in the project.
3. The joins table, the part no doc had: for each route or action, the fields the UI sends, the fields the schema accepts, the handler, the tables it touches, its tests. A mismatch is flagged in the overview: a field sent but dropped, a write route with no auth or CSRF check, a handler nothing calls, a file too big to read whole (over 1,500 lines).
4. A project's own generators: a list of commands under "map" in the kit config (French's `pnpm carte`); the map runs them and links their output from the area's card.
5. Fresh or refused: the map records the commit it was built from, and `kit.py map --check` fails when the code changed since; tests in tests/test_map.py on small Python and TypeScript fixtures, with scripts/kit_map.py.
6. The real case, read-only: build the map of ~/french into a scratch folder (never write in ~/french). Its overview fits one screen; the game's area card names the engine, the round screen and the action route; the joins table flags the dropped `feuilles` field and the teams route with no CSRF check.

Bars: how many of the audit's three join bugs the map flags (out of 3), the overview's length in lines, the build time on ~/french. Keep `map` in the kit's command index.
title: A map of any project, generated from its code
verdict: Yes: the map of ~/french fits in 50 lines, flags all three of the audit's join bugs, names the engine, the round screen and the action route on the game's card, and builds in 30 s without writing anything in ~/french.
